text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Tuesday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Chairman of the Latvian Unity Party Albert Kauls announced that at its conference on March 15 the party will decide on a merger with the Democratic Party Saimnieks.

- Chairman of Democratic Party Saimnieks Ziedonis Chevers voiced his support to the candidature of Robert Zile as candidate to the post of finance minister. He also said that despite the recent growth of the Saimnieks faction they have no intention to revise the structure of the cabinet.
- The press office of Latvia's foreign ministry reports that delegations of Latvia and Russia resumed talks on the delimitation of the interstate border and discussed a draft agreement on the issue.
- On March 3 a special department will start functioning within the State Audit with the task of controlling the use of funds by local governments.
- Parliament's revision committee has revealed several irregularities in the use of funds allocated to repair parliament's building.

- The welfare ministry started a vaccination programme against diphtheria, which is sponsored by the International Red Cross and the government of Italy. So far the disease has claimed 55 lives but only 44 percent of the population has been vaccinated.

- Several transit business associations have sent an open letter to Prime Minister Andris Shkele drawing his attention to several cases when cargoes were seized and confiscated by Riga customs office illegally.

- The president of Ventspils Nafta, Janis Blazhevich, announced at a press conference that the visit of the Latvian delegation headed by Alfreds Chepanis to Moscow is of crucial importance for Latvian business.
- Riga airport manager Dzintars Pomers spoke about plans to extend the airport's runway as well as to rebuild and extend the existing passenger terminal and build a new cargo terminal.
- Norway's Varner Hakon plans to build a building construction materials trading centre in Riga at a cost of at least $3 million.
